Reconfiguring/renewing the WAN interface should re-establish internet flow.

data.component: WAN uplink / WAN interface session on gw.lan (vtnet0)
data.cause: The internet dropped at ~02:01 because the ISP link failed (cable modem lost sync: "No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out", then a config-file/TFTP failure causing a modem re-registration); the modem is back to OPERATIONAL since ~02:28, but gw.lan's WAN session was left stale because the watchdog runs in observe mode and never applied the reload it decided on at 02:30/02:40, leaving traffic to the ISP gateway (198.51.100.1) black-holed.
evidence: ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 from gw.lan: 100% packet loss to the ISP-side gateway, although 'arp -a -n' shows it resolving (00:17:10:9a:a3:96) — path broken beyond the LAN

cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl: 02:01:44 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out', 02:14:10 'TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND', 02:28:21 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete' — outage originated at the ISP/modem side and resolved before now

cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl: status NOT_SYNCHRONIZED at 02:06, OPERATIONAL by 02:29 and still OPERATIONAL at 02:40 (with elevated uncorrected codewords), so the modem itself is fine now
tail /var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: watchdog decided 'reload' at 02:30 and retried at 02:40 but only logged 'would_reload' because mode=observe, so no WAN renewal actually happened
cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json: outage_start 1772521560 (~02:06 local), 2 reloads recorded, last_action reload — consistent with a stale WAN session through the recovery

ifconfig vtnet0 shows WAN UP/RUNNING with lease 198.51.100.27 (cat /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0, renew not due until 2026/3/5), while LAN-side ping to 10.20.0.9 succeeds — local services/network are healthy
data.recommendation: Reconfigure/renew the WAN interface on gw.lan (wan_reload was requested and its preconditions were met) so the firewall re-establishes its WAN session with the now-registered modem; if outages like this recur, consider taking the watchdog out of observe mode so it applies the reload automatically, and have the ISP check the upstream plant given the T3 timeout and rising uncorrected codeword counts.
